risk_note: RV2 (identity second verification and auxiliary endpoints; BR-ID-04 细则 authorization attempts, BR-ID-08 step-up, BR-ID-12 / BR-ID-13 consents, BR-ID-32 h5_token; 04 §6.1). Authorization attempts live in Redis for the configured lifetime, are bound to provider / purpose / device_id (step_up also uid and action) and are consumed only after every check passed, atomically. Step-up by SMS verifies and consumes a purpose=step_up code of the bound phone; the third-party branch checks and consumes the attempt first and then asks an exchange port (default unavailable → 50305; the real exchange is CT-15i), refusing an identity other than the account's bound union_id. step_up_token (aud=step_up, 300 s) is only issued here; consumption is the business endpoints'. h5_token (aud=h5, default read_only, 900 s, bound to sid) is accepted by the token check only outside the signed / auth / withdrawal / payout-account / phone / deletion routes, read_only only on GET, and dies with its session. Consents insert only; withdrawing privacy is always device level and revokes the device's sessions, install_secret and push tokens in one transaction. Contract: four x-implementation: planned lines removed, route-schemas regenerated. Version gate and deletion_only scope are B1-03c's. Full verification by the required CI checks (ops/approvals.yaml id 21).

reviews.scope: independent read-only Claude subagents: round 1 pass with four S2 (h5 principal scope fixed to full — B1-03c; hand-written h5 exclusion prefixes; privacy withdrawal needs neither signature nor token — contract design, follow-up contract task; lock order of withdrawal vs createSession, fixed in round 2); round 2 pass with no findings (Codex's S1 verified solved: lockUserConsents serialisation plus row_version conditional update, no lock-order cycle; x-auth none routes unchanged without a valid h5 token; 10403 envelope per contract); out-of-scope: Apple refresh_token storage (CT-15i), login_merge not syncing users.personalization_off (existing B1-02j code)

reviews.note: round 1 fail (S1 concurrent personalization consents could leave users.personalization_off inconsistent with the latest record; S2 app_id of the token not checked against the signing device, read_only h5 token not restricted on x-auth none routes, HEAD treated as read) fixed in round 2 (user consent lock + row_version conditional update, 10403 on app mismatch, read-only enforcement on x-auth none routes with a valid h5 token, GET only); round 2 pass, checklist complete, one S2 (a read_only h5 token posting to /v1/auth/h5-token gets a plain 10403 without data.reason — recorded in followups)

spec_test_review.note: rule tests by Codex (3 rounds) reviewed by fresh Claude subagents: round 1 fail (S1 fixture X-App-Id longer than the contract allows made every red a fixture red; S1 a consumed SMS code answers 20003 not 20002; S2 nonce entropy; S2 h5 scope narrower than BR-ID-32), round 2 pass after Codex round 2; orchestrator-approved exception round pass after Codex round 3 changed one expectation (a revoked device's signed request is 10402 per the frozen B1-03a signature check); the three Codex rounds were squashed by the orchestrator into one test commit
